📖 Matnni o‘qing:

A comprehensive meta-analysis has delivered a severe blow to a long-standing claim in experimental psychology. Rarely has the discipline experienced so comprehensive a refutation of a once-dominant theoretical framework. Not only did the meta-analysis undermine the initial claim, but every subsequent preregistered replication has likewise failed to recover the effect. Were the analytic flexibility to have been constrained a priori, the contradictory pattern of results might have been anticipated. So endemic were the questionable research practices—chiefly the unrestricted use of convenience samples drawn from WEIRD populations and undisclosed analytic decisions—that the majority of the published literature is now regarded as provisional.

Had the sampling frame not been restricted to WEIRD populations, the external validity of the inference would have been markedly higher. It is essential that all preregistrations be deposited prior to data collection and that deviations be transparently reported. The editorial board recommended that the analysis be re-executed with a family-wise error correction and that the raw data be made available. The reported effect is held in abeyance by multiple independent laboratories that have been unable to replicate it under stricter protocols. Notwithstanding the battery of robustness checks, alternative explanations involving residual confounding remain viable. What the literature currently lacks is not further correlational reports but a programme of adversarial collaborations and preregistered experiments. No sooner had the corrected analysis been posted than three additional groups confirmed the same direction-reversing coding error.
